root_cause: analyze_param() in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py branches on the annotation type first. If the annotation is a special injected type (Request, WebSocket, HTTPConnection, Response, StarletteBackgroundTasks, SecurityScopes), it runs `assert depends is None, "Cannot specify `Depends` for type ..."`. So `Annotated[Response, Depends(f)]` and `response: Response = Depends(f)` raise an AssertionError when the route is defined, even though the explicit Depends should win. This regressed when Annotated support landed in 0.95.0.
best_solution: In analyze_param, guard the special-type branch with `depends is None and lenient_issubclass(type_annotation, (Request, WebSocket, HTTPConnection, Response, StarletteBackgroundTasks, SecurityScopes))` and delete the `assert depends is None` line inside it. With an explicit Depends, control falls through to the normal dependency path: the dependency is called, and its return value is injected (it can be the injected Response, or a new JSONResponse the endpoint then returns). With no Depends, the old special injection still happens. The field_info assert stays, so `Annotated[Response, Query()]` is still rejected. The statement says exactly this: 'check for Depends before applying special type handling'.
acceptable_alternatives: Any reordering that puts the `depends is not None` check ahead of the special-type check, e.g. an early `if depends is not None: <dependency path>` before the lenient_issubclass block. Keeping the assert and only special-casing Response would fail the BackgroundTasks test (test_background_tasks_with_depends_annotated).
hidden_test_demands: New file tests/test_response_dependency.py, 7 tests: test_response_with_depends_annotated and test_response_with_depends_default (X-Custom header set by the dependency shows up in the response); test_response_without_depends (plain injection still works); test_response_dependency_chain (Annotated[Response, Depends(second)] where second itself takes Annotated[Response, Depends(first)], both X-First=1 and X-Second=2 present); test_response_dependency_returns_different_response_instance (dependency returns a new JSONResponse, the endpoint mutates and returns it, X-Custom=='modified'); test_request_with_depends_annotated; test_background_tasks_with_depends_annotated (Annotated[BackgroundTasks, Depends(add_task)] runs tasks from both the dependency and the endpoint). The BackgroundTasks test means the fix has to cover every special type, not just Response.
locating_signals: The statement names the function (`analyze_param()`), quotes the exact assertion text ('Cannot specify `Depends` for type Response'), and describes the fix ('check for Depends before applying special type handling'). Grepping the assertion string finds the single line in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py.
our_outcome_summary: Solved by all four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8 all kaggle_env_pass=true). All four made the same source change as gold, byte-identical apart from gold's two comment lines: add `depends is None and` to the special-type condition and delete the assert. v4/v6 changed source only (791 chars, 58-61 s, 20-22 calls). v7/v8 also added their own tests/test_response_dependency.py (the hidden test's path, which the hidden test_patch overwrites). That was harmless but cost more time: v8 took 98 s and 42 calls.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement quotes an assertion or error message and says which check should come first, grep for the literal message, move the guard condition into the branch predicate, and delete the assert. Change nothing else. Keep the fix general across the whole tuple or class list the branch covers, because hidden tests often exercise sibling types (here BackgroundTasks and Request, not just the Response named in the title). Don't spend calls writing your own tests at a path the hidden tests will overwrite.
